task4_cell_key.question: Could the key (sector, raw printed fixed point n_a) ever SPLIT one physical fixed point into two keys, hiding a same-cell doubling?
task4_cell_key.answer: NO. Decisively excluded on both geometries.

decisive_test.method: number of DISTINCT printed n_a per sector over the ENTIRE raw census, versus the number of SIMULTANEOUS affine point-group orbits of the sector's 6d fixed-point set (GeomMN.sim_orbits, the certified alphabet_survey phase-2 engine; its docstring: '#sim_orbits must equal the number of constructing elements the file prints for that sector')

Z3xZ6_1_1.(1,1)/(1,2)/(1,3)/(2,1): 0 printed; these are the CPT partners of (2,5)/(2,4)/(2,3)/(1,5) and their orbit counts match those partners exactly (6/15/6/3)

decisive_test.result: BIJECTIVE in every populated sector of both geometries. No split, no merge.

unrotated_plane_entries.measured_over: every field record of the full raw census, both geometries
unrotated_plane_entries.result: orbifolder prints (0,0) in the two lattice coordinates of an unrotated plane in 100% of records. Z2xZ4: plane 2 in T(0,1),T(0,2),T(0,3); plane 1 in T(1,0); plane 3 in T(1,2); T(1,3) has no unrotated plane. Z3xZ6: plane 2 in T(0,l); plane 1 in T(1,0),T(2,0); plane 3 in T(1,4),T(2,2).
unrotated_plane_entries.consequence: the N=2 direction contributes no spurious key coordinate, so it cannot split a cell

false_alarm_recorded.finding: a PER-PLANE orbit reading reports 1 apparent collision on Z2xZ4 T(0,2) and 5 on Z3xZ6 (T(0,2), T(0,4), T(2,4)x3)
false_alarm_recorded.why_it_is_not_a_split: a per-plane orbit label is strictly coarser than the space-group conjugacy class, because the conjugating point-group element acts on all three planes simultaneously. Worked example: Z2xZ4 T(0,2), rotation diag(-1,+1,-1); the Z4 generator swaps the plane-1 fixed points e1/2 <-> e2/2 AND the plane-3 pair simultaneously, so (A,A)~(B,B) and (A,B)~(B,A) are two classes while the per-plane reading merges them. 4 singletons + 2 + 2 + 2 = 10 simultaneous orbits = 10 printed keys.
false_alarm_recorded.supporting_evidence: d5_keysplit.py: the colliding key pairs carry identical V_g = p_sh mod Lambda and identical |p_sh|^2 multisets in every model (495/495, 252/252, 241/241, 290/290, 284/284, 289/289) -- as required for fixed points in one per-plane orbit -- which is why only the simultaneous-orbit count settles the question.

task4_cell_key.verdict: The cell key is COMPLETE in the sense of CLAUDE.md 5.22 first addendum (ii) and cannot hide a doubling. This is a positive certification the phase did not have.

task5c_records_versus_states.finding: verify.py:216-241 (and the certified g1d_crosstab.py:48-50) count RECORDS per (cell, role). A hidden non-singlet record is several distinct massless left-chiral states at the same cell with the same SM role -- and orbifolder's own SMConfig table counts them that way (printed[...] += row[3]).
task5c_records_versus_states.why_it_matters: two states of one hidden multiplet differ by a hidden root: Delta in Lambda, Delta orthogonal to the SM Cartan span, |Delta|^2 >= 2, |p|^2 = |p'|^2. The theorem therefore requires R >= 1/2 for such a record. Since the measured 10-role R on Z2xZ4 is at most 17/40 < 1/2, the theorem PREDICTS that no twisted 10-role field can be a hidden non-singlet -- a sharp test the phase's own counter cannot perform.

result.interpretation: every one of the 10,621 hidden non-singlet 5bar records sits at R = 7/10 or 33/40, both >= 1/2; every one of the 4,038 records at R = 13/40 or 3/40 (< 1/2) is a hidden singlet. Zero exceptions on 312,050 fields.

task5c_records_versus_states.verdict: The absence claim SURVIVES the record-vs-state attack and is STRENGTHENED by it: the theorem's untested corollary (no 10-role field may be a hidden non-singlet) holds 67,555/67,555, and the hidden-multiplicity/R correlation holds with zero exceptions. But 6.1's 5bar multiplicity histogram is a record histogram presented as a field-multiplicity histogram, and the correct state-level histogram is different.

task6_I1_as_a_check_on_delta_c.structure: I1 tests |p_sh|^2/2 = 1 - delta_c(k,l) - N_osc with |p_sh| PRINTED by orbifolder, N_osc read from the PRINTED oscillator string, and delta_c computed from the hard-coded v1, v2 in verify.py's GEOM dict.
strength: It is over-determined: one delta_c per sector against thousands of independently printed p_sh. Z2xZ4 T(1,2) alone pins delta_c against 48,236 role-carrying fields.

Every populated sector contains oscillator-free fields (measured: the maximal B in each sector's B_by_sector histogram is realised, e.g. Z2xZ4 T(0,1) {13/16: 13605, 9/16: 1934}), so delta_c is pinned WITHOUT reliance on the oscillator convention in every sector -- the N_osc term is not free to absorb a delta_c error.
p_sh is not computed by this phase at all, so a delta_c error would have to be matched by a systematic error in orbifolder's own printed shifted momenta.
blind_spots: delta_c = sum_a x_a(1-x_a)/2 with x = v mod 1 is INVARIANT under v -> -v plane by plane, and under any permutation of the three planes. I1 therefore cannot detect a conjugated or plane-permuted twist -- exactly the CLAUDE.md 5.19 family. Any statement that attributes a B value to a NAMED sector or plane inherits that blindness.
I1 is a per-sector scalar identity; it constrains the SUM delta_c + N_osc, and only the presence of oscillator-free fields (verified above) separates the two.
I1 was evaluated only on the 481,728 role-carrying fields, not on the full spectrum -- and on Z3xZ6 it therefore also excludes the 4,309 hidden-non-singlet SM-role fields (task5b).
task6_I1_as_a_check_on_delta_c.decisive_point: delta_c IS NOT LOAD-BEARING FOR THE MEASUREMENT. verify.py:220 computes B = S.dot(p_sh, p_sh)/2 from the PRINTED p_sh, and R = 2B - |w|^2 (line 224). delta_c appears only in the I1 comparison at line 222-224 and nowhere else. The loophole cells are selected by R computed from p_sh, and their sector labels come from orbifolder's printed 'sector (k,l)'. So attack #7's worry -- delta_c and p_sh wrong in a correlated way -- cannot move any verification number, any violation count, any R histogram, or the 65 loophole fields. It could only damage the NARRATIVE that attributes the B windows {11/16, 3/4, 13/16} and {31/36, ...} to particular sectors and twists (sections 3.4 and 7).
task6_I1_as_a_check_on_delta_c.verdict: I1 is a genuine and strong cross-check against a random delta_c error, blind to delta_c-preserving twist transformations (conjugation, plane permutation), and -- more importantly -- irrelevant to the safety of the measurement, because the measurement never uses delta_c.

defects.title: 'independent pipeline ... shares no code beyond the parser' is false
defects.detail: verify.py calls the certified census's parse_spectrum, parse_gauge_factors, parse_smconfig, observable_positions and role_census (Z2xZ4) / parse_spectrum, parse_gauge, observable_positions, role_census (Z3xZ6) -- the same functions the certified g1d_crosstab.py calls, in the same order, with the same cfgs[0] selection. Only the ~5-line tally is fresh. The reproduction confirms the counting layer, not the role assignment.
defects.fix: restate as 'reproduced through the same certified SM-identification pipeline; the tallying layer is independent', and say explicitly that the role assignment is NOT independently verified by this reproduction.

defects.fix: rename the rows to '(cell, role) pairs' and add the distinct-cell counts; correct the certified gate by dated addendum.

defects.title: 6.1 and 6.2 are not the same measurement -- the Z3xZ6 library drops hidden non-singlets
defects.detail: 4,309 Z3xZ6 SM-role field records (hidden multiplicity 2/3/4/5) are assigned role=None and vanish from the census; all 4,309 are 5bar-family, none 10-family. The Z3xZ6 5bar totals, the 169,678 role-carrying-field count and the I1 coverage all exclude them; the Z2xZ4 equivalents include theirs. Second inconsistency: z24's net() weights by hidden multiplicity, z36's counts records.
defects.impact: the 10-role absence claim is UNAFFECTED (0 of 4,309 are 10-family; re-running with the gate removed produces 0 new 10-role doublings). The Z3xZ6 5bar numbers are understated.
defects.fix: state the definition each geometry's number uses, or re-run Z3xZ6 without the gate.

defects.title: the per-cell counter counts records, not states
defects.detail: hidden non-singlet records are several states at one cell with one role. Correct Z2xZ4 5bar state-level histogram is 1:189,003 2:29,723 3:2,198 4:81, not 1:198,429 2:21,664 3:910 4:2.
defects.impact: GATE-VERIFIED SAFE for the letter: all 67,555 Z2xZ4 ten-role records are hidden singlets, so record and state counts coincide there; state-level theorem test returns 0 violations on both geometries. And the omission concealed a POSITIVE result -- the theorem's untested corollary (no 10-role field may be a hidden non-singlet, since R <= 17/40 < 1/2) holds 67,555/67,555, and no hidden non-singlet of any family sits at R < 1/2 (0 of 312,050).
defects.fix: report the state-level histogram and add the hidden-multiplicity corollary as a confirmed prediction.

defects.title: '615 closure-failed, excluded and reported' -- 599 of them are censusable
defects.detail: 599 of the 615 print a LATER vev-configuration that closes; only 16 are genuinely unclosable. Same shape as CLAUDE.md 5.22 first addendum (i).
defects.impact: coverage gap of 599/11,540 = 5.2% of the catalogue. CLOSED BY THIS GATE: recovered and censused, 4,910 additional 10-role (cell,role) triples, all multiplicity 1, 0 hits.
defects.fix: select the SM configuration by closure over ALL printed configurations, not cfgs[0]; quote 11,524 closable models.

defects.title: gate attack #3's premise is answerable and benign
defects.detail: every excluded model prints k_Y = 5/3 on every generator (615/615 Z2xZ4, 2/2 Z3xZ6). The k_Y > 5/3 permissive-threshold worry is empty.

defects.title: Z3xZ6 model labels are not globally unique
defects.detail: MSSM0..MSSM9 each occur twice across segments (4,622 blocks, 4,612 distinct labels). verify.py records `model=lab` in violations/loophole_cells, so a reported cell is not uniquely addressable on that geometry. No model is lost or double-counted.

defects.title: the |w|^2 projection is not independent of the shared role labels
defects.detail: section 9 says |w|^2 was 'obtained by explicit projection rather than inferred from k_Y'. True -- but the SM Cartan span it projects onto is selected using role_census's own Q/dc/L/Hu labels (qrec, drec, lrec), so the projection inherits the shared role assignment.

overall: No fatal defect. The two totals ARE the same quantity in both pipelines and reproduce, but the pipeline is not independent (D5-1) and the quantity is misnamed (D5-2). The cell key is certified bijective with the physical cells on both geometries -- it cannot hide a doubling. The excluded set is safe on k_Y by measurement and its recoverable 97.4% has now been censused with zero hits. Two attacks the phase could not run -- record-vs-state and the hidden-multiplicity corollary -- both pass and STRENGTHEN the letter.
